content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am reaching out regarding an issue with an older [product_name] device. I have a USB cable to connect the [product_name] to my PC, but when attempting communication, I receive the error: "Can not go to IP address com x." The drivers are properly installed and visible in the device manager. Any help is appreciated. I apologize for my English, as I am French.
You need to connect using: Interface Connect through: [product_name] Select cable, and then choose the relevant COM interface.
Thank you for your response, but that's already what I did. Please see the attached image.
Are you certain that COM9 is the correct port? Which cable are you using? Is it an original [company_name] one or a different brand?
If I recall correctly, there may be an issue with special characters in the COM port name (such as accent circonflexe).
That issue only occurs with the Ethernet interface name. On the left side of your screenshot, there's the French name for the [product_name] cable.

I've attached a screen recording. I still use an old [article_no] device. For communication, I have an old [company_name] RS232 cable and a USB / RS232 adapter from Digitus. No manual driver installation is required. The drivers install automatically when you plug in the adapter. The virtual COM interface, COM5, appears and disappears with the adapter.
The cable is detected by the device manager on COM9. It isn't a [company_name] cable, but rather a CH340-compatible one.

I'm not sure if the CH340 chipset works properly with the [product_name] software. My Digitus USB/RS232 adapter uses an FTDI chipset, and as shown in the video, the [product_name] software works without problems. Keep in mind you won't receive support for non-original [company_name] cables, which is the drawback of using third-party products.
Thanks for your reply. I've reached the same conclusion—hardware incompatibility. I will look into getting an original [company_name] cable.

Unfortunately, an original cable from [company_name] can cost as much as a new [product_name]. You may want to consider purchasing a new [product_name] device. With only an Ethernet patch cable needed, you can update or upgrade the software for free, and the latest [product_name] version offers more features and memory.
A new [product_name] with Ethernet wouldn't be problematic. I just wanted to reuse my old device, but it seems both it and the cable may end up discarded.
That seems like the best solution.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing problems connecting an older [product_name] module to a PC using a non-original USB cable. The [product_name] software fails to establish a connection when using a CH340-based adapter, producing COM port-related errors. Original cables from [company_name] or some third-party adapters with FTDI chipsets reportedly work reliably. This highlights compatibility challenges with generic hardware, causing user frustration due to limited support and ambiguous hardware guidance.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect smooth and dependable PC communication with [product_name] devices using any USB cable, as long as drivers are installed and a supported COM port is selected, without hardware compatibility issues.
